question: I am sorry. I want to know if IBM Cloud provides a service for  financial instituions.

answers: Yes, IBM Cloud provides a service called IBM Cloud for Financial Services. This service is designed to help financial institutions meet the strict security and regulatory requirements of the financial industry. It includes a variety of features and tools to help financial institutions build, deploy, and manage secure and compliant cloud applications. The IBM Cloud Framework for Financial Services outlines the controls that services must comply with to be designated as IBM Cloud for Financial Services Validated. This validation indicates that the service has demonstrated compliance with the framework's controls and can be used to build solutions that may themselves be validated.

history.content: How do I create persistent volume claims?

To create a persistent volume claim (PVC) in Kubernetes, you can follow these steps:
1. First, you need to have a Persistent Volume (PV) available. This PV can be created manually or dynamically provisioned by a storage class.
2. If you have a manual PV, you can create a PVC by using a YAML file with the appropriate specifications. Here's an example of a PVC YAML file:
  apiVersion: "v1"
  kind: "PersistentVolumeClaim"
  metadata:
    name: "pvcvsan0   f crawler-pv-nfs.yaml                                                                                                                                            you also can create on the following message is displayed:
persistentvolume/jdoe-nfs-pv created 3. Create a file called crawler-pvc-nfs.yaml with the following content:
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata: name: spec: accessModes:  ReadWriteMany resources: requests: storage: 10Gi selector: matchLabels: pv-name:
Replace the following variables:
    : Specify the name of your persistent volume claim. For example, jdoe-nfs-pvc.
    : Specify the name of your persistent volume. For example, jdoe-nfs-pv.
    Enter the following command to create the persistent volume claim:
oc create -f crawler-pvc-nfs.yaml
What is  a persistent volume claim

A Persistent Volume Claim (PVC) is a request for storage resources in Kubernete and before you can crawl a local file system, you must create  a persistent volume claim and mount it on the crawler pod. You also need to copy the files that you want to crawl to the Discovery cluster that you are working on.Before you get started with provisioning storage, it is important to understand the Kubernetes concepts for storage, dynamic provisioning, static provisioning, as well as the storage classes that are available to you.

It is also a container orchestrator to manage the lifecycle of containerized apps in a cluster of worker nodes.

Red Hat OpenShift is a Kubernetes container platform that provides a trusted environment to run enterprise workloads. It extends the Kubernetes platform with built-in software to enhance app lifecycle development, operations, and security. With OpenShift, you can consistently deploy your workloads across hybrid cloud providers and environments. It offers a more opinionated and managed approach compared to vanilla Kubernetes, with additional features for application development, deployment, and management.
Can i have an IBM Cloud account?

Yes, You can sign up for an IBM Cloud account by using an existing IBMid or by creating a new IBMid.    You can get an IBM Cloud infrastructure account by upgrading your IBM Cloud account to a billable account, or by linking your existing IBM Cloud infrastructure account with your IBM Cloud account.  When you create the account it i  highly recommended that you use a functional ID that is owned by your company rather than an employee's personal ID. A functional ID is a company-owned email address (such as ibm-cloud-admin@domain.com) used to represent a functional user. This allows for uninterrupted administrative access by the account owner as employees leave the company or are reassigned to other projects    .              I
Educational institutions, can they have IBM Cloud?

Yes, educational institutions can provide IBM Cloud account to their students so that they can learn valuable skills through hands-on projects that use IBM Cloud services. The university has a complete view of the costs of each department and course.

How do I know that my data is safe? 

Designed with secure engineering practices, the IBM Cloud® platform provides layered security controls across network and infrastructure. IBM Cloud focuses on protection across the entirety of the compute lifecycle, which includes everything from the build process and key management to the security of data services. IBM Cloud also provides a group of security services that can be used by application developers to secure their mobile and web apps. These elements combine to make IBM Cloud a platform with clear choices for secure application development.

In addition to our own diligence in creating and operating a secure cloud, IBM® also engages many different firms to assess the security and compliance of our cloud platform. For more information, see [IBM Cloud compliance programs](https://www.ibm.com/cloud/compliance) for a detailed list of certifications and attestations.

Storing and encrypting data in Security and Compliance Center 

To ensure that you can securely manage your data when you use IBM Cloud® Security and Compliance Center, it is important to know exactly what data is stored and encrypted, and how you can delete any stored personal data.

For more information about how IBM Cloud platform secures your data, see [How do I know that my data is safe?](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/overview?topic=overview-security)



  How is my configuration data obtained?

You can sign up for an IBM Cloud account by using an existing IBMid or by creating a new IBMid.
* IBM Cloud infrastructure account. This account is used to log in to the IBM Cloud infrastructure customer portal that provides some additional function to manage infrastructure products and services. You can get an IBM Cloud infrastructure account by upgrading your IBM Cloud account to a billable account, or by linking your existing IBM Cloud infrastructure account with your IBM Cloud account. The IBM Cloud infrastructure account that you are using must meet certain requirements. For more information, see [Signing up for required accounts](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/vmwaresolutions?topic=vmwaresolutions-signing_required_accounts).



* How do I associate my IBM Cloud infrastructure credentials with the VMware Solutions console?
